title: Compass manifest.yml
description: The manifest. Lives at .compass/work/<issue-slug>/manifest.yml. The human-readable companion is manifest.reference.yml.

schema_version.description: The Compass issue.yml schema version this file follows. The CLI warns/fails on incompatible versions. Optional in 1.0 for back-compat; recommended. '1.1' introduced the optional `status` and `land_timestamp` fields.

issue.description: The issue slug; matches the directory name. A manifest still carrying the retired root key loads - normalize_spine maps it forward through SPINE_KEY_MAP before anything reads it, and cli/migrate-map.yml records the pair.

task.description: RETIRED. Declared only so a manifest written before the rename does not trip additionalProperties on its way to the normaliser, which maps it to `issue`. Never written.

created.description: ISO date the issue was assessed.

status.description: Optional. Lifecycle status of the issue. 'active' (default when absent) means in-flight; 'queued' means recorded as next up but not started; 'parked' means stopped with the phases so far still valid, so it can resume; 'landed' means ship completed and its scenarios are eligible for the living system spec derivation (ADR-008); 'abandoned' means it will not resume. Only 'landed' grants derivation eligibility - every other value is ineligible, so a new value can never silently get it. Issues with schema_version '1.0' that lack this field are treated as 'active', for backward compatibility.

landed_by.description: Optional, and only meaningful on a landed issue. What delivered this issue's work, when the work happened somewhere else. Each entry names another issue or a commit. When it resolves, four checks about this issue carrying its OWN record stand down - the claim moves to whatever carries the evidence rather than being waived. An issue entry must name an issue that exists, has landed, carries a record, and names this one back in `delivered:`; a commit entry must resolve in the project's repository and say what it did. See the `landed-by-resolves` check.

issue.description: Slug of the issue that delivered this work. That issue must name this one in its `delivered:` list - the link is two-way, or anything could claim anyone's evidence.

commit.description: A commit in the project's own repository that delivered this work. The common case: most already-done issues were fixed by an ordinary commit with no issue opened.

what.description: Required alongside `commit`. What that commit did, in words. A bare sha is a reference nobody can act on, and on a shallow clone nobody can resolve.

delivered.description: Optional. Slugs of other issues whose work this issue delivered. The back-reference for `landed_by`: without it a pointer is one-way, and any issue could claim a landed issue's record for the price of typing a slug that exists.

tracked_at.description: Optional. URL of the public issue tracking this work. The archive under .compass/work/ is not published, so a queued issue that anyone outside the repository needs to see is raised as a GitHub issue and linked from here.

land_timestamp.description: Optional. ISO 8601 timestamp of when the issue was landed. Written by scripts/integrate.sh alongside status: landed. Used as the primary sort key for the living spec derivation order (ADR-008 §3).

land_commit.description: The commit ship-commit made when it marked the issue landed. evidence-matches-tree compares the newest green's tree_id with this commit's tree.

subtasks.description: The subtasks of a multiagent run, written only by `compass issue subtask`. Each records the files that crossed a boundary, the base commit, model, budget and cost, and the progress a resume needs. Optional: a manifest without it loads.

brief.description: The brief file the builder was handed.

earlier_briefs.description: The briefs of earlier dispatches of this subtask, kept when a later one records its own.

report.description: The result file the builder returned (named result.md; a subagent is refused a file named like a report).

review_brief.description: The reviewer's brief. Refused when registered if it matches a fixed list of phrases that say what not to flag.

package.description: The latest review package: the diff from base_sha, one file per dispatch.

base_sha.description: The full id of the commit the builder started from.

cost.description: Tokens the dispatch used. Over the budget adds a finding.

reviewed_revision.description: The commit the latest review read.

review_rounds.description: Every review round, appended. The fix-round cap is sized from these later.

assessment.description: The four-dimension assessment the assess stage produces.

delivery_approach.description: The final delivery approach; filled by `compass approach evaluate --write`.

orchestration.description: Whether this issue is delivered by a single agent or by several. Set at breakdown, once the distribution map says whether independent subtasks exist; assess does not write it - see subtask_ceiling. Manifests written before ADR-023 carry the retired key name, which is read forward through cli/migrate-map.yml.

subtask_ceiling.description: How many parallel subtasks this delivery approach permits, written by `compass approach evaluate`. A ceiling, not a decision: the evaluator has no concept of a work unit.

stages.description: stage name -> weight string; filled by approach evaluate.

evidence.description: The issue's evidence registry - typed, id-tagged entries gates reference by id. Built incrementally across stages.

id.description: Stable id, e.g. EV-001 or EV-A1.

path.description: Path to the evidence file (relative to the issue dir, or absolute).

scenario.description: Scenario id this evidence is FOR (when applicable).

scope.description: For human-approval: what the approval is for.

decision.description: For human-approval: pending | approved | rejected. For spike-conclusion: discard | graduate-to-delivery | defer.

conditions.description: For human-approval: any conditions attached to the approval.

next_task.description: For spike-conclusion with decision=graduate-to-delivery: the path to the new issue that owns the delivery work (e.g. .compass/work/<new-slug>/).

record_id.description: The identity of the record this entry was created from. Stamped into the record at write time and copied here, so `evidence-identity-matches` can ask whether the file a gate cites is still that run. Absent on entries written before stamping existed - those are unverifiable, never verified.

content_digest.description: A digest over the record's content when this entry was created. A matching record_id with a differing digest means the record was edited in place rather than replaced.

gates.description: Seeded by approach evaluate (status pending); each stage updates the gates it clears.

evidence.description: When status is `pass`, a list of evidence ids referencing entries in the top-level `evidence` registry. `null` or empty until cleared.

scenarios.description: The machine-readable index of acceptance-criteria.md; filled by the define stage.

intent.description: The intent id(s) this scenario traces to - a string or a list of strings (a scenario may serve more than one intent).

group.description: Independence group seeding the distribution map.

verifiable.description: Scenario taxonomy, e.g. 'narrative' for a documentation-as-acceptance playbook.

superseded_by.description: Optional. Scenario id(s) that replace this one. behaviour-mapping names silent supersession as an anti-pattern: a target scenario replacing a behaviour-mapped baseline is a recorded decision, not a silent overwrite. Without the link a reader cannot tell a baseline that failed because the change landed as intended from one that failed because something broke.

changed_files.description: Every production file the issue changes, each traced to >=1 scenario id; filled at implement.

claims.description: Public/marketing claims, each traced to a backing scenario; filled by `/compass:position`.

follow_ups.description: Work this issue deferred and still owes (e.g. a hotfix's). `compass check` fails while any is unresolved. The v2 states are outstanding/resolved; the 1.x spellings (owed/paid) stay schema-legal so an unmigrated manifest still lints - readers normalise them.

target_task.description: Cross-issue follow-up: the issue whose ship is blocked until this is resolved.

paid_at.description: Optional audit field: when the follow-up was resolved.

paid_note.description: Optional audit field: a note recorded when resolving.

reassessments.description: Append-only log of re-assessments, written by `compass approach evaluate --write --reason`. Feeds the assessment calibration signal that `compass retro` reads.

kind.description: What kind of re-assessment this was. Only 'judgement' feeds compass retro's re-sizing signal - a policy correction or a scope change is not the assessment having misread the work.

changed.description: What the recomputation actually moved - delivery approach, stages, gates, orchestration - each as a from/to pair. Written by the evaluator as the audit detail behind the reason.

friction.description: Optional. Written at ship. Records where Compass's own process weight cost more than it returned between assess and ship, and how the framework could have been configured to avoid it. A strategy-class signal (soft, advisory) - never gates ship. Absent on issues that hit no friction; nothing happens for a project that never writes it (ADR-006). Aggregated by `compass retro --friction`.

phase.description: The stage the friction was felt in.

category.description: What kind of friction this was.

observation.description: What got in the way, stated concretely.

proposed_change.description: How the framework could have been configured to avoid it - the aggregation key.

source.description: derived: assembled automatically at ship from the reassessments log. human: given by the author.

repairs.description: hotfix approaches only: the slug of the issue this hotfix repairs. Read by `compass retro --impact` to compute the change-fail signal. Optional - a hotfix that declares none is reported as a coverage gap rather than silently counted as zero.

parked_reason.description: Optional. Why a parked issue was set aside - the thing a reader needs to decide whether to resume it.

evaluated_assessment.description: Optional. The assessment `compass approach evaluate --write` last computed from. Written by that command and read only by the next run of it, to notice a corrected dimension when the computed approach absorbs the correction. Not a second source of truth: `assessment` holds the four dimensions, and this is a copy of what was last evaluated.

status_reason.description: Optional. Why the status was last changed, for any status other than parked - a re-opening, an abandonment, a landing out of the usual order. Written by `compass issue set-status --reason`. Parking has its own key because a parked issue is the one a reader most often has to decide about.

parked_at.description: Optional. ISO-8601 timestamp recording when the issue was parked.

artifacts.description: The issue's artifact registry: which documents this issue produced, where they are, and WHY each exists - or why it was deliberately not written. The reason is the point. A filename with no reason is a directory listing, so `reason` is required on every entry including the omitted ones. The CLI resolves a registered `path` first and the flat filename beside the manifest second, so an issue with no registry keeps working. An old entry, written before paths became project-relative, holds a bare filename. That filename no longer resolves from the registry, but the CLI still finds it beside the manifest and says that is how it found it, so an unmigrated entry is visible rather than silent. `compass migrate` rewrites them.

kind.description: What kind of document this is - technical-design, intent, threat-model.

path.description: Where the document is, as a path measured from the PROJECT ROOT - not from the issue directory. That is what lets a human-facing document live under `docs/compass/<date>-<slug>/` while the manifest stays under `.compass/work/<slug>/`. A path that resolves outside the project is refused rather than read. Absent on an omitted entry, which has no document. NOTE: the `evidence:` registry is the other way round - its paths stay relative to the issue directory, because evidence does not move.

status.description: `omitted` is the one that makes a decision visible: paired with a required reason, it records that a document was deliberately not written rather than forgotten.

reason.description: Why this document exists, or why it was omitted. Required either way.

revision.description: Optional. Bumped when the document materially changes; an approval binds to it.
